verdict.rationale: Lovable's Git sync lets you clone the repo, edit/commit locally (i.e., with your own coding agent or IDE tooling) and push changes that sync back into the Lovable project, which is a real but indirect way to have an external agent drive changes alongside the built-in agent. However, there is no first-class 'connect your agent' integration inside the builder itself—the only agent-connection feature documented is the reverse direction (exposing a Lovable app as an MCP server for external assistants to call, not letting an external agent operate the builder). missing for 10: a native way to plug in an external coding agent (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) as the driver inside Lovable's own UI/session, and any hands-on evidence that git-sync-based external editing behaves like 'driving the builder' rather than just external code contribution.
